title.es: 28 de abril de 2025 · Por qué cayó la red

en: April, twenty twenty-five. The Iberian peninsula loses power.
Phones still show coverage, but messages stop leaving.
The mobile network does not fall with the lights.
Each mast runs on its own battery, and the batteries run dry one by one.
Within hours, stable connections drop from ninety percent to forty.
Those hours are a warning window. Today, nobody uses them.
es: Abril de 2025. La península ibérica se queda sin luz.
Los móviles siguen mostrando cobertura, pero los mensajes no salen.
La red móvil no cae al irse la luz.
Cada antena tira de su batería, y las baterías se agotan una a una.
En pocas horas, las conexiones estables caen del 90 al 40 %.
Esas horas son una ventana de aviso. Hoy nadie la aprovecha.

title.es: 29 de octubre de 2024 · DANA de Valencia

en: October, twenty twenty-four. The Valencia floods.
The extreme rain fell upstream, in the hills.
In many of the towns that flooded, it was barely raining.
The water came down the ravines, towards people who could not see it coming.
The mass alert reached phones at eleven minutes past eight in the evening.
Why so late is still disputed. The lesson: measure upstream, warn downstream.

La alerta masiva llegó a los móviles a las 20:11.
Por qué tan tarde sigue en disputa. La lección: medir arriba, avisar abajo.

title.es: 18 de enero de 2026 · Adamuz

en: January, twenty twenty-six. Adamuz.
A train derails and invades the other track. A second train hits it.
The first calls carried the position of the first train only.
It took around forty-five minutes to learn there was a second one.
Hundreds of passengers' phones felt the impact. That reached nobody.
The preliminary investigation points to a broken rail weld; it is still open.

title.es: El mismo patrón, siempre

en: Behind every case, the same pattern.
The network falls after the event, not during it.
The official alert depends on the mobile network: exactly what fails.
The data that could warn us already exists. Nobody connects it.
And silence gets misread: a phone that does not answer is not a victim.
Yet every phone already carries radios, a speaker, a microphone and sensors.

Y el silencio se malinterpreta: un móvil que no responde no es una víctima.
Y cada móvil ya lleva radios, altavoz, micrófono y sensores.

title.es: Qué instalas

en: You don't need an app store. You open a web address once, with a connection.
It installs on the phone and from then on works with no network at all.
In an emergency, three big buttons: I'm safe, I need help, I'm trapped.
Your message is encrypted on your own phone, in about three hundred bytes.
Only the person it is meant for can read it.
On Android it is also a real app, with everything inside.
No browser, and no network needed even to start it.

title.en: Phone to phone · store, carry, forward
title.es: De móvil a móvil · guardar, llevar, reenviar

en: Without a network, every phone running SENDA becomes a relay.
It carries other people's messages, sealed, unable to read them.
When two phones meet, they swap what they are carrying.
A car, a bus, a person walking: anything that moves becomes a courier.
When the message arrives, a signed receipt travels back
and erases the copies still circulating. A fake receipt is ignored.
Tested in the lab: a city of forty phones, delivering only by encounters.
es: Sin red, cada móvil con SENDA se convierte en un relé.
Lleva mensajes ajenos, sellados, sin poder leerlos.
Cuando dos móviles se cruzan, intercambian lo que llevan.
Un coche, un autobús, alguien andando: todo lo que se mueve hace de mensajero.
Cuando el mensaje llega, vuelve un recibo firmado
que borra las copias que siguen circulando. Un recibo falso se ignora.
Probado en laboratorio: una ciudad de 40 móviles que entregan solo al cruzarse.

title.es: Un mensaje, muchos caminos · Reed-Solomon

en: SENDA never bets on a single channel. It cuts every message into fragments.
Reed-Solomon coding adds spare ones: send ten, and any six rebuild it exactly.
They leave at once by satellite, LoRa radio, drones and neighbours.
If a path dies, the others are enough.
In a simulation of 200 sends with bearers dropped at random, 198 were rebuilt.
Which paths to use is decided by Contact Graph Routing, from space networking:
the earliest arrival over every chain of contacts, several routes in parallel.
es: SENDA no apuesta por un solo canal. Corta cada mensaje en fragmentos.
Reed-Solomon añade repuestos: envías diez y seis cualesquiera lo rehacen.
Salen a la vez por satélite, radio LoRa, drones y vecinos.
Si un camino muere, los demás bastan.
En una simulación de 200 envíos perdiendo portadores al azar, se rehicieron 198.
Qué caminos usar lo decide Contact Graph Routing, de las redes espaciales:
la llegada más temprana por toda cadena de contactos, varias rutas en paralelo.

title.es: Arnhem → San Martín de Valdeiglesias

en: A real question: I live in the Netherlands.
My brother is in Spain, and his mast is down.
WhatsApp delivers when his phone gets its own coverage back.
SENDA looks for any real bridge: a neighbour with satellite Internet,
another operator still running, a nearby phone over Bluetooth.
In this simulation: SENDA in about four minutes. WhatsApp, in eight hours.
With no bridge at all, SENDA does not pretend: it waits for the first window.
If only your operator fails, 112 still works through any other operator's mast.

title.en: The network reserve · an Internet battery

en: Your phone also keeps a reserve: one gigabyte by default.
While there is Wi-Fi, it stores what you will need offline:
maps, shelters, your emergency plan, satellite orbits, your documents.
An exact optimisation chooses by value, local risk and how fast it goes stale.
What you need to send waits in a queue, and goes first in the next short window.
Stored bytes are not coverage. But they keep the app useful with no network.

title.en: Physics · why rain cuts some radios
title.es: Física · por qué la lluvia corta unas radios

en: Now the physics. Why does rain cut some links and not others?
It depends on the size of a raindrop compared with the radio wave.
At 868 megahertz the wave is about thirty-five centimetres long.
Drops barely touch it: in heavy rain, it loses almost nothing.
At 28 gigahertz the wave is about one centimetre: the size of a drop.
It loses about seven decibels per kilometre.
So in storms, SENDA prefers low bands.
Model ITU-R P.838, computed by the app itself, at fifty millimetres per hour.
es: Ahora, la física. ¿Por qué la lluvia corta unos enlaces y otros no?
Depende del tamaño de la gota comparado con la onda de radio.
A 868 megahercios la onda mide unos 35 centímetros.
Las gotas apenas la tocan: con lluvia fuerte, casi no pierde nada.
A 28 gigahercios mide un centímetro: el tamaño de una gota.
Pierde unos siete decibelios por kilómetro.
Por eso, en tormenta, SENDA prefiere bandas bajas.
Modelo ITU-R P.838, calculado por la propia app, a 50 mm por hora.

title.es: Física · la radio sobre una montaña

en: A mountain does not block radio completely. The wave bends over the ridge.
That is diffraction. SENDA computes it on real terrain by two classic methods.
A ridge sixty metres above the line between two points ten kilometres apart
costs about twenty-two decibels at 868 megahertz.
Knowing the loss tells us where one relay on a hilltop restores the link.
es: Una montaña no bloquea la radio del todo. La onda se curva sobre la cresta.
Es la difracción, y SENDA la calcula sobre relieve real con dos métodos clásicos.
Una cresta sesenta metros por encima de la línea entre dos puntos a diez kilómetros
cuesta unos veintidós decibelios a 868 megahercios.
Conocer la pérdida dice dónde un relé en lo alto recupera el enlace.

title.es: Satélites, cuando pasan

en: Satellites are not always overhead. SENDA computes their orbits on the phone,
predicts each pass, and treats it as one more contact for the router.
Low orbits for short messages; medium orbits for position and rescue beacons.

title.es: Prever el apagón

en: Back to the blackout. SENDA models how long each mast lasts on battery
and maps where and when people will lose coverage, before it happens.
Then it chooses where to place gateways, with a mathematical guarantee.
In the test city, five gateways reach seventy-two percent of those cut off.

Después elige dónde poner pasarelas, con garantía matemática.
En la ciudad de prueba, cinco pasarelas llegan al 72 % de los aislados.

title.en: Roads · the braking you cannot see
title.es: Carretera · la frenada que no ves

statLabel.es: coches que chocan · resultado del modelo

en: In Spain, 1,119 people died on interurban roads in 2025.
Fog, a hundred and twenty kilometres an hour, one point two seconds between cars.
Each driver reacts to the brake lights ahead. The delays add up: five cars crash.
With SENDA, the first phone detects the braking and warns everyone behind at once.
In the model, only the tailgater still crashes. Only a safe distance fixes that.
With no coverage, the SOS rides with passing cars: out in seven minutes,
in simulation, with only one car in ten running SENDA.
es: En España, 1.119 personas murieron en vías interurbanas en 2025.

Con SENDA, el primer móvil detecta la frenada y avisa a todos los de detrás.
En el modelo, solo choca el que iba pegado. Eso solo lo arregla la distancia.
Sin cobertura, el SOS viaja con los coches que pasan: sale en siete minutos
en simulación, con solo uno de cada diez coches con SENDA.

title.en: You stop to help · protect, alert, help
title.es: Paras a ayudar · proteger, avisar, socorrer

en: If you stop at an accident, SENDA guides you with the DGT routine:
protect, alert, help.
It tells 112 where you are in their words: road, kilometre point and direction,
even inside a tunnel, and using landmarks such as wind turbines.
Each task is confirmed by another person.
When the Guardia Civil arrives, it takes command and receives the summary.

incluso en un túnel, y usando referencias como los aerogeneradores.
Cada tarea la confirma otra persona.
Cuando llega la Guardia Civil, toma el mando y recibe el resumen.

title.es: Trenes · segundos, no minutos

statLabel.en: to identify the second train · simulation
statLabel.es: en identificar el segundo tren · simulación

en: Back to the train. Every phone on board can feel the impact:
speed, a violent stop, a phone tipping over. Drops and braking are ruled out.
It asks: are you all right? If there is no answer in twenty to thirty seconds,
that silence is itself vital information for rescuers.
SENDA fuses hundreds of reports: how many trains, which coaches, how many trapped.
In simulation, the second train is identified in thirty to forty seconds,
with a quarter of passengers; with one in twenty, under a minute.
The summary goes out in CAP, the format 112 control rooms already read.
es: Volvamos al tren. Cada móvil a bordo puede sentir el impacto:
velocidad previa, parada brusca, vuelco. Se descartan caídas y frenadas.
¿Estás bien? Si no hay respuesta en veinte o treinta segundos,
ese silencio ya es un dato vital para el rescate.
SENDA fusiona cientos de avisos: cuántos trenes, qué coches, cuántos atrapados.
En simulación, el segundo tren se identifica en 30 a 40 segundos,
con un cuarto de los pasajeros; con uno de cada veinte, en menos de un minuto.
El resumen sale en CAP, el formato que ya leen las salas del 112.

title.es: Terremotos · segundos de aviso

en: No one can predict an earthquake. But once it starts, it can be detected.
The first wave, the P wave, is fast and weak. The destructive S wave comes later.
Each phone's accelerometer watches for the P wave on its own.
With four phones or more, the network locates the epicentre
and counts the seconds before the S wave reaches each town.
In synthetic data, fourteen phones locate it within half a kilometre.
One unofficial source triggers nothing: a public catalogue must confirm.
es: Nadie puede predecir un terremoto. Pero cuando empieza, se puede detectar.
La primera onda, la P, es rápida y débil. La destructiva, la S, llega después.
El acelerómetro de cada móvil vigila la onda P por su cuenta.
Con cuatro móviles o más, la red localiza el epicentro
y cuenta los segundos hasta que la onda S llega a cada pueblo.
Con datos sintéticos, catorce móviles lo sitúan con medio kilómetro de error.
Una fuente no oficial nunca activa nada: lo debe confirmar un catálogo público.

title.es: Inundaciones · medir arriba, avisar abajo

en: For floods, SENDA turns rainfall into river flow with classic hydrology,
includes the reservoirs, and watches how fast the water rises upstream.
In a synthetic scenario, the warning leaves two and a half hours
before the first town floods: a town where only three litres per square metre fell.

En un escenario sintético, el aviso sale dos horas y media
antes de que se inunde el primer pueblo, donde solo cayeron tres litros por metro.

title.en: Wildfires · warn before the mast burns
title.es: Incendios · avisar antes de que arda la antena

statLabel.es: de margen de aviso perdido · simulación

en: In a wildfire, SENDA computes the spread with wind, slope and fuel,
and crosses its arrival time with every phone mast and every town.
Here, the mast serving the town burns one hundred and seven minutes
before the deadline to warn it.
So the alert must leave earlier, or travel by mesh, LoRa and satellite.
es: En un incendio, SENDA calcula el avance con viento, pendiente y combustible,
y cruza su hora de llegada con cada antena y cada pueblo.
Aquí, la antena que da servicio al pueblo arde ciento siete minutos
antes del límite para avisarlo.
Así que la alerta debe salir antes, o viajar por malla, LoRa y satélite.

title.es: Edificios derrumbados · desde fuera

en: When nobody can enter a building, a drone climbs the façade floor by floor,
listening to the Bluetooth beacons that phones emit, without connecting to them.
Phones change address every few minutes,
so SENDA counts how many are active at the same time.
Across 720 simulated floors, its margin held the real figure 95 % of the time.
Under rubble, five phones hear a knock
and place it within ten centimetres, in simulation.
A phone that does not answer is listed as missing, unconfirmed. Never as a victim.
es: Cuando nadie puede entrar en un edificio, un dron sube la fachada planta a planta,
escuchando las balizas Bluetooth de los móviles, sin conectarse a ellos.
Los móviles cambian de dirección cada pocos minutos,
así que SENDA cuenta cuántos hay activos a la vez.
En 720 plantas simuladas, el margen acertó la cifra real el 95 % de las veces.
Bajo escombros, cinco móviles oyen un golpe
y lo sitúan a diez centímetros, en simulación.
Quien no responde figura como desaparecido sin confirmar. Nunca como víctima.
en_say: When nobody can enter a building, a drone climbs the facade floor by floor,
listening to the Bluetooth beacons that phones emit, without connecting to them.
Phones change address every few minutes,
so Senda counts how many are active at the same time.
Across seven hundred and twenty simulated floors, its margin held the real figure ninety-five percent of the time.
Under rubble, five phones hear a knock
and place it within ten centimetres, in simulation.
A phone that does not answer is listed as missing, unconfirmed. Never as a victim.

title.es: Coordinadores y organismos

en: Who can send alerts? Only an agency, with its own trust anchor,
signing credentials for its coordinators.
A coordinator marks a zone and sends a signed order:
siren, beacon, sensor report, evacuation.
Each phone checks the signature, the zone and its owner's consent before acting.
Residents answer with one tap.
The coordinator sees a board, building by building, floor by floor.
SENDA never impersonates the official alert.
It carries it where the network no longer reaches.
es: ¿Quién envía alertas? Solo un organismo, con su propia ancla de confianza,
que firma las credenciales de sus coordinadores.
Un coordinador marca una zona y envía una orden firmada:
sirena, baliza, informe de sensores, evacuación.
Cada móvil comprueba firma, zona y permiso de su dueño antes de actuar.
Los vecinos responden con un toque.
El coordinador ve un cuadro por edificio y por planta.
SENDA nunca suplanta la alerta oficial.
La lleva donde la red ya no llega.

signing credentials for its coordinators.
A coordinator marks a zone and sends a signed order:
siren, beacon, sensor report, evacuation.

title.es: Más personas, red más fuerte

en: Like other decentralised networks, SENDA does not depend on a central server.
Every phone is a node: the more people use it, the denser the mesh.
Anonymous delivery receipts teach the network which channels work, area by area,
and those counts merge between phones without any central server.
It reads open sources too: USGS and GDACS for disasters, Copernicus imagery,
MET Norway weather, and traffic from the DGT and the Dutch NDW in DATEX II.
Sources that copy each other never count as independent confirmation.
es: Como otras redes descentralizadas, SENDA no depende de un servidor central.
Cada móvil es un nodo: cuanta más gente lo usa, más densa es la malla.
Los recibos de entrega anónimos enseñan a la red qué canales funcionan en cada zona,
y esos recuentos se combinan entre móviles sin servidor central.
También lee fuentes abiertas: USGS y GDACS para desastres, imágenes de Copernicus,
meteorología de MET Norway y tráfico de la DGT y el NDW holandés en DATEX II.
Las fuentes que se copian entre sí nunca cuentan como confirmación independiente.

Anonymous delivery receipts teach the network which channels work, area by area,
and those counts merge between phones without any central server.
It reads open sources too: U S G S and G D A C S for disasters, Copernicus imagery,
MET Norway weather, and traffic from the D G T and the Dutch N D W in DATEX two.
Sources that copy each other never count as independent confirmation.

title.es: Funciona con lo que ya existe

en: The same core runs on a phone, a computer, an agency server,
a drone or an emergency vehicle.
Alerts in CAP. Traffic in DATEX II. Drones over MAVLink.
Car data over OBD-II, with the owner's consent.
Navigation apps, carmakers and wind farms connect through official agreements.
Never by breaking into anyone's systems.
es: El mismo núcleo funciona en un móvil, un ordenador, el servidor de un organismo,
un dron o un vehículo de emergencias.
Alertas en CAP. Tráfico en DATEX II. Drones por MAVLink.
Datos del coche por OBD-II, con permiso del dueño.
Apps de navegación, fabricantes y parques eólicos se conectan por convenio oficial.
Nunca entrando en sistemas ajenos.
en_say: The same core runs on a phone, a computer, an agency server,
a drone or an emergency vehicle.
Alerts in C A P. Traffic in DATEX two. Drones over MAV-link.
Car data over O B D two, with the owner's consent.
Navigation apps, carmakers and wind farms connect through official agreements.
Never by breaking into anyone's systems.

title.es: Módulos de pocos euros

en: And it grows with cheap hardware. An ESP32 board turns a mast or a drone
into a Wi-Fi and beacon scanner. Its firmware is already built in CI.
We are designing more from off-the-shelf parts: a 24 gigahertz radar
that sees a person moving, even through smoke;
a micro-seismograph for river bridges; a solar LoRa repeater.
Estimated parts cost: five to twenty euros each. Designed, not yet field-tested.
es: Y crece con hardware barato. Una placa ESP32 convierte un mástil o un dron
en un escáner de wifi y balizas. Su firmware ya se compila en CI.
Diseñamos más con piezas de catálogo: un radar de 24 gigahercios
que ve moverse a una persona, incluso entre humo;
un microsismógrafo para puentes de río; un repetidor LoRa solar.
Coste estimado en piezas: de 5 a 20 euros. Diseñados, aún sin probar en campo.
en_say: And it grows with cheap hardware. An E S P thirty-two board turns a mast or a drone
into a Wi-Fi and beacon scanner. Its firmware is already built in C I.
We are designing more from off-the-shelf parts: a twenty-four gigahertz radar
that sees a person moving, even through smoke;
a micro-seismograph for river bridges; a solar LOR-ah repeater.
Estimated parts cost: five to twenty euros each. Designed, not yet field-tested.

title.en: Verified by machine · honest about what is missing
title.es: Verificado por máquina · honesto con lo que falta

en: Every change is checked by machine: 496 core tests,
and 49 end-to-end checks, almost all with the network cut.
Built with an engineering corps of 43 specialised AI agents,
independent red teams, and one rule: never invent.
What is missing, we say: field pilots with real phones and rescue teams,
an independent security audit, and certification for public procurement.
Next: a pilot with civil protection, a gateway to 112, and a mobile operator.
es: Cada cambio se comprueba por máquina: 496 pruebas del núcleo
y 49 comprobaciones de extremo a extremo, casi todas sin red.
Construido con un cuerpo de ingeniería de 43 agentes de IA especializados
equipos rojos independientes y una regla: no inventar.
Lo que falta, lo decimos: pilotos de campo con móviles reales y equipos de rescate,
una auditoría de seguridad independiente y la certificación para compra pública.
Siguiente: un piloto con protección civil, una pasarela al 112 y un operador móvil.

and forty-nine end-to-end checks, almost all with the network cut.
Built with an engineering corps of forty-three specialised A I agents,
independent red teams, and one rule: never invent.
What is missing, we say: field pilots with real phones and rescue teams,
an independent security audit, and certification for public procurement.
Next: a pilot with civil protection, a gateway to one one two, and a mobile operator.
